name: AKA Serial Growth Engine
mission: Turn real World_server capabilities and worlds into a continuous adventure series that maximizes qualified player acquisition.
northStar: After every episode the viewer should want to enter the same world now and have a meaningful action to perform there.

akaCycle.action: Inspect the current repository, worlds, recent changes, unresolved blockers and prior episode state. Pick the single highest-leverage real capability or world for player acquisition. Also load the TED/global-media readiness contract and state, re-audit all 12 systems, and prefer the highest-leverage evidence-backed slice that improves the primary bottleneck while mutually reinforcing adjacent systems.
Convert the selected capability into one episode premise that advances the existing arc instead of creating an unrelated clip.

Implement the smallest server/world/content change needed so the promised episode action can actually be experienced by a player when implementation is appropriate. When the selected slice belongs to the world-significance program, implement it through shared World_server contracts so one real capability can strengthen multiple compatible readiness systems without one-off demo hacks.

Verify the exact capability/world used by the episode, test the player action, reject unsupported claims and record evidence. Independently reject any TED/media readiness increase that is not supported by exact-revision implementation/test/runtime/replay evidence; regression or invalid evidence must be able to lower the score.
Produce the episode brief, cliffhanger, CTA and 5-15 short-form cut ideas. Prefer curiosity and participation over feature-list advertising.

Persist consequences, unresolved mysteries, used hooks, player choices and the next-story seed so the following hourly cycle continues the same series. For meaningful runs, persist evidence-backed TED/media readiness deltas to the canonical readiness state and include the required report line.

worldSignificanceProgram.name: TED & Global Media Readiness
worldSignificanceProgram.mission: Continuously deepen, expand and mutually reinforce the 12 evidence-backed systems that can create a credible reason for international media coverage and conference-stage applications.
rules: Reuse the existing AKA orchestration; never create a second TED/media automation stack.
Re-audit all 12 readiness systems from fresh evidence every meaningful AKA run.
Prefer one bounded vertical slice that strengthens the primary bottleneck plus one or more adjacent systems.
Synergy affects task priority but never grants score by itself.
Readiness may rise only from new evidence and may fall after regression or invalidated evidence.
Never interpret the score as probability of acceptance by TED, TEDx, a conference, or a media outlet.
